alt: Original midsize SUV 2002-2009; unrelated small crossover 2021-2026 (not sold 2010-2020)

issues.t: Original SUV: fuel gauge reads wrong
issues.sym: The fuel gauge shows empty when the tank is full, sticks, or jumps around, sometimes with the low fuel light on.
issues.why: Sulfur in fuel can foul the contacts on the fuel level sender inside the tank. GM offered special coverage for some model years that has since expired.
issues.next: Use the trip odometer to track fuel until it is fixed. The repair involves replacing the sender in the tank.

issues.t: Original SUV: electric fan clutch failure
issues.sym: Overheating in traffic or while towing, a check engine light, or a fan that roars all the time.
issues.why: The electronically controlled fan clutch can fail or stick, so the fan does not pull enough air at low speed.
issues.next: Watch the temperature gauge and stop if it climbs. Have the fan clutch and its wiring tested.

issues.t: Original SUV: power window regulator failure
issues.sym: A window grinds, pops, moves slowly, or drops into the door.
issues.why: The cable and plastic guides in the window regulator wear out or break.
issues.next: Replace the regulator. Avoid using the window if it is falling, and secure it closed.

issues.t: Original SUV: blower runs on one speed or keeps running
issues.sym: The fan works only on high, does not work at all, or keeps running after the engine is off.
issues.why: The blower motor control module or resistor fails.
issues.next: Have the blower control module tested and replaced if needed.

issues.sym: Speedometer, fuel, or temperature gauges stick, read wrong, or drop to zero.
issues.why: The small stepper motors that move the gauge needles inside the instrument cluster wear out.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: you may not see your speed or warning lights, so ease off, keep a safe distance, and pull over where it's safe. Restarting the car once parked may bring the display back; if it doesn't, have it fixed before you drive again. Have the cluster repaired or replaced. Do not rely on a faulty temperature gauge to warn you of overheating.

issues.t: Crossover: turbo wastegate rattle and low boost
issues.sym: A rattle at cold start, a check engine light, and less power than usual.
issues.why: The turbocharger wastegate linkage can wear. GM issued a bulletin and special coverage for some 1.2L models.
issues.next: Ask a dealer whether the special coverage applies to your VIN and have the turbo inspected.

issues.t: Crossover: infotainment screen freezes or reboots
issues.sym: The touchscreen freezes, restarts on its own, or phone connections drop.
issues.why: Software faults in the radio unit. GM released software updates.
issues.next: Ask a dealer to install the latest radio software.

issues.t: Original SUV: driver door window switch can overheat and burn (recall)
issues.sym: Power windows or locks that work on and off, a hot or burning smell from the driver door, or smoke from the switch panel.
issues.why: Water and road salt can get into the driver door switch module and corrode it, causing a short that can start a fire even when the vehicle is parked and off.
issues.next: If it happens while you're driving: if you smell burning or see smoke, pull over where it's safe, turn the engine off, get everyone out and well away from the car, and call 911 if there are flames. Don't drive it again until it has been repaired. Park outside until the recall is confirmed done. A dealer can check the VIN and replace the door module.

issues.t: Original SUV: headlights can go out from a failed driver module (recall)
issues.sym: Low beams and daytime running lights that cut out or will not come on.
issues.why: The headlamp driver module can overheat and fail, shutting off the low beams.
issues.next: Have a dealer check the VIN and replace the module. Avoid night driving if the headlights are cutting out.

issues.t: Crossover: loss of power brake boost (recall)
issues.sym: A brake warning message and a pedal that suddenly needs much more force to stop the car.
issues.why: Contamination on a sensor inside the electronic brake booster can interrupt the boost.
issues.next: If the brake pedal suddenly turns hard or a red brake warning comes on, press the pedal much harder than normal, slow down, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on — call for a tow. The brakes still work but need a hard push. Stop driving and have a dealer check the VIN and the brake booster.

issues.t: Crossover: front seat rear bolts may be missing (recall)
issues.sym: A front seat that rocks, shifts or clunks when you brake or accelerate.
issues.why: Some vehicles left the factory without the rear attachment bolts on one or both front seats.
issues.next: Have a dealer inspect the seat mounting and check the VIN before carrying on as normal.

issues.sym: No symptom while driving. The risk is when lifting the car to change a tire.
issues.why: The supplied jack can fracture if it is not placed exactly as the owner manual shows, letting the vehicle drop.
issues.next: Do not get under the car on the factory jack. Ask a dealer whether the jack recall applies to your VIN.

issues.t: Crossover: backup camera image blank or distorted (recall)
issues.sym: The screen shows a black, scrambled or missing picture when you shift into Reverse.
issues.why: A fault in the rear camera system can keep the image from displaying correctly.
issues.next: Use your mirrors and look behind you when backing up, and have a dealer check the VIN for the camera recall.

issues.t: Crossover: camshaft cover leak with oil burning
issues.sym: Oil has to be added between changes, a puff of blue smoke shows at startup or on the highway, and there may be an oily smell.
issues.why: The plastic camshaft cover on these small turbo engines can crack or lose its seal, which lets oil get pulled into the intake and burned.
issues.next: Have the oil level checked and the cover inspected. Keep the oil topped up until it is repaired so the turbo is not starved.

issues.t: Crossover: CVT damage when the fluid gets low
issues.sym: Slipping, a whine or belt-like noise that rises with speed, shuddering, or the car suddenly will not pull.
issues.why: The continuously variable transmission on front-drive models relies on a steel chain and pulleys. If the fluid level drops, the chain and pulley faces score and wear quickly.
issues.next: Stop driving if it slips or whines. The fluid level and the chain have to be checked before the whole unit is ruined.

issues.t: Crossover: sudden loss of drive from the valve body
issues.sym: The car loses power or will not move, often with a message about reduced propulsion and a warning light.
issues.why: A stuck or leaking valve in the transmission valve body drops the pressure needed to hold a gear, so the transmission cannot send power to the wheels.
issues.next: Do not keep driving it. Have the transmission scanned for codes and the valve body inspected; software updates are also part of the fix.

issues.t: Crossover: rear door weatherstrip comes loose
issues.sym: Wind noise at highway speed, a rubber seal hanging away from the rear door opening, or water on the door sill.
issues.why: The rear side door weatherstrip can pull out of its channel where the glue or clips let go.
issues.next: Have the seal reseated or replaced. It is not a safety problem, but it lets in noise and water.
